irrbbDisclosureNote: Scotiabank discloses IRRBB every quarter in its Report to Shareholders MD&A (Table T23 'Structural interest sensitivity'), and again at fiscal year-end (Oct 31) in the Annual Report (Table T50) and the audited financial-statement notes. It shows only two prescribed shocks — an immediate, sustained +100bp and -100bp parallel rate shock across major currencies — not the full Basel/OSFI six-scenario set (no steepener, flattener, or short-rate shocks are separately disclosed publicly). Both ΔEVE (present value of net assets) and ΔNII (next-12-month net interest income) are shown, pre-tax, on a constant balance-sheet basis with no management-action mitigation assumed, broken out by Canadian dollar vs. other currencies. Scotiabank states results are within 'Board-approved limits' but does not disclose those limits or express the sensitivities as a percentage of any capital measure — the %-of-Tier-1-capital figures in this dataset are computed by us, not sourced directly.
irrbbDisclosureSourceName: Scotiabank Q3 2025 Report to Shareholders, MD&A, Table T23 'Structural interest sensitivity' (also Annual Report Table T50 at year-end)
